newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf makes proposals on strike, unions to consult.
newsitem.headline: Elf makes proposals on strike, unions to consult.

text.p: Oil firm Elf Aquitaine said that it had made proposals aimed at easing a week-old French refinery strike on Thursday and that unions would consult their members.
But a union official, while confirming consultations would take place on Friday, said a three-hour negotiating session with Elf had failed to address the main issue of jobs.
"Things went well," an Elf spokesman told Reuters after the talks at Elf's Paris headquarters.
"Management made proposals which the unions will discuss and we will see tomorrow if work starts again or not," he said.
But Claude Henry, coordinator at the moderate CFTC trade union, one of five unions in the talks, said he was not satisfied with the outcome.
"I am not satisfied because the big problem is employment," he said.
"I don't know whether the strike will continue or not. That is up to the employees to decide," he said.
The strike, which has brought Elf's three French refineries to a standstill for eight days, was originally sparked by plans to cut 330 jobs in Elf's French refining division, Elf Antar.
It has since blown into a wider dispute over other demands including shorter hours, more pay and early retirement.
France's largest union, the CFDT, said before Thursday's talks it would only negotiate on pay, which Elf agreed to discuss, if job cuts were shelved in advance.
Elf refused, Henry said. There was no immediate comment on the issue from Elf management.
Henry said all unions would consult the refinery strikers overnight and on Friday morning on Elf's proposals.
He said these included a 1.5 percent real salary increase in July next year, an immediate salary bonus of 2,500 francs and a plan to allow some refinery shift workers to retire at 56.
They had called for retirement at 55 in line with a deal won by French truckers in a 12-day nationwide protest last week.
Another type of bonus known as the "progress bonus" would be maintained, instead of scrapped as Elf has proposed.
Other unions were not immediately available to give their reaction to the proposals.
Three Elf refineries with a combined capacity of 440,000 barrels per day are involved in the strike.
They are the Grandpuits plant near Paris, Feyzin outside Lyon and Donges, a major coastal refinery in western France.

Oil traders said earlier Elf had been forced to buy over 100,000 tonnes of gasoline on the international oil market and divert or sell millions of barrels of unused crude oil as a result of the refinery strike.
-- Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
